::: {#def-logistic-regression}

#### Logistic regression

A **logistic regression** model for binary outcomes $\outvar_1, \dots, \outvar_n \in \set{0, 1}$
with predictor vectors $\vpredvar_1, \dots, \vpredvar_n$
says that the outcomes are [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) and that

$$
\Prf{\Outvar_\iobs = 1 \mid \vpredvar_\iobs} = \prob_i
= \sigmoidf{\dprod{\vcoef}{\vpredvar_\iobs}},
\qquad
\sigmoidf{u} = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-u}},
$$ {#eq-logistic-model}

where $\vpredvar_\iobs = \tp{\paren{1, \predvar_{i1}, \dots, \predvar_{ip}}}$ and $\vcoef = \tp{\paren{\coef{0}, \coef{1}, \dots, \coef{p}}}$.
The leading $1$ in $\vpredvar_\iobs$ makes $\intcoef$ the intercept, and $\coef{j}$ for $j \ge 1$ is the slope for the $j$th predictor.

Source: @wikipedia_logistic_regression.
:::
